name: Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre
overview: Indigenous community-controlled art centre in Yirrkala, Northern Territory, about 700 km east of Darwin, serving Yirrkala and about 25 homeland centres within 200 km (stated by the centre).

Founded in 1976 when Yolŋu artists set up Buku-Larrŋgay Arts in the old Mission health centre, as the Methodist Overseas Mission withdrew. The centre was formerly called Buku-Larrŋgay Arts (Wikipedia). The beachfront gallery that Narritjin Maymuru opened in the 1960s is counted among its inspirations.
The Mulka Project, a digital archive and production studio, was added in 2007 (stated by the centre).
funding_verdict: Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre: mixed: federal arts support, self-generated sales, and grants from the Ian Potter Foundation and the Cotton On Foundation

press_items.title: Ian McLean, review of "Yolŋu Power: The Art of Yirrkala" (2025)

name: Kunstraum Dornbirn
overview: Contemporary art venue in the Stadtgarten park of Dornbirn, Vorarlberg, at Jahngasse 9, with its office at Marktstraße 33 (Kunstraum website).
Founded in 1987 as a private non-profit association to present and communicate contemporary art; it has shown in the historic assembly hall since 2003 (Kunstraum website).

The Dornbirn turbine maker Rüschwerke built the brick hall in 1893 to assemble its ever larger turbine wheels; the company closed in 1984, and when the site was remodelled from 1999 to 2000 into the Stadtgarten, which also holds the inatura museum, the hall was left unchanged (Kunstraum website).
funding_verdict: Kunstraum Dornbirn: mainly public: the City of Dornbirn, Land Vorarlberg and the Republic of Austria, with Dornbirner Sparkasse
wider_context: In March 2012 Gerald Matt, then director of the Kunsthalle Wien since 1996, asked to end his contract after a three-month suspension over allegations of mixing private and official work and of citizenships promised for sponsorship (ORF Wien, 2012).

In December 2012 the Economic and Corruption Prosecutor's Office (WKStA) dropped its investigation of Matt for attempted prohibited intervention and breach of trust, finding that the interventions were not confirmed; it said much of the breach-of-trust complaint had become time-barred (ORF Wien, 7 December 2012).
The WKStA also dropped its investigation of Thomas Häusle, then president of the Kunsthalle Wien association (ORF Wien, 7 December 2012).
Matt now presides over the Kunstraum Dornbirn board and Häusle directs it.

name: Ars Electronica Center
overview: Media-art and technology museum at Ars-Electronica-Strasse 1, 4040 Linz (Ars Electronica website).

Ars Electronica began as a festival in Linz in September 1979, founded by Hannes Leopoldseder, Hubert Bognermayr, Herbert W. Franke and Ulrich Rützel. Ars Electronica Linz GmbH was incorporated as a company in 1995 and the Center and the Futurelab research group opened in 1996 (Wikipedia).

The new Center opened on 2 January 2009 after about two years of construction at a cost of about 30 million euros, designed by Treusch architecture, with a 5,000 square metre glass skin of 1,100 panels fitted with LEDs (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Ars Electronica Center: mixed: City of Linz and Upper Austria, federal funds, EU project money, corporate partners and self-earned income

"KissMyArs", "The tireless enchantment of technological sorcery | Ars Electronica 2016 Review" (14 August 2016)
Elvia Wilk, "transmediale 2015: Why we need spaces for art and tech beyond corporate influence" (18 February 2015)

name: MAK - Museum of Applied Arts
overview: Applied arts, design, architecture and contemporary art museum at Stubenring 5, in Vienna's Innere Stadt (Wikipedia; museum website).

Founded in 1863 under Emperor Franz Joseph I with Rudolf von Eitelberger as first director. It opened in 1864 in temporary rooms and moved in 1871 into its purpose-built Neo-Renaissance building by Heinrich von Ferstel (Wikipedia).
Lilli Hollein has directed it since 2021, its first female director (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: MAK: mainly public: base funding (Basisabgeltung) of 11.7 million euros, plus ticket, rental and sponsorship income
wider_context: Radio Free Asia (Alim Seytoff and Roseanne Gerin, 27 November 2024) reported that Volkswagen sold its operations in Xinjiang, a joint-venture plant in Urumqi with SAIC. Activists and experts had accused VW of allowing Uyghur forced labour there; VW said in December 2023 that its audit showed no signs of human rights violations, and Adrian Zenz judged the audit "unsuited to meaningfully assess the presence or absence of forced labor".
Porsche Holding Salzburg, the MAK's partner since 2024, is owned by Volkswagen AG (Wikipedia).

press_items.title: W24 Redaktion, "Nach Millionenraub im MAK: Kritik an Sicherheitsvorkehrungen" (31 August 2026)

name: Azerbaijan National Museum of Art
overview: Art museum at Niyazi street 11/9 in central Baku.
Created in 1936, when the Council of People's Commissars of the Azerbaijan SSR made the art department of the Azerbaijan State Museum an independent museum (Wikipedia); AzerNews gives 1937.
It occupies two 19th-century buildings, one of them the De Bour mansion, which it entered in 1951; a glass and steel passage joined them in 2013.
funding_verdict: Azerbaijan National Museum of Art: unconfirmed: a state museum by its 2011 national status
wider_context: In July 1993 artworks were stolen from the museum and later recovered (Wikipedia).

name: Al Riwaq Art Space
overview: Non-profit art and design hub in the historic Bank House at Al Guful, Manama, that describes itself as a campus for art and design.

Opened in 1998 as a commercial gallery in a modest villa in the Adliya district, run by director Bayan Al Barrak Kanoo, and later became an art space and then a non-profit (the space's own history; The National, 11 June 2015, calls it "now a not-for-profit organisation"). Monocle says Kanoo moved to Bahrain from Baghdad in the mid-1980s and began by selling work by Iraqi artists.
Building: since 2022 the Bank House in Al Guful, called "historic" by the space. The pages read name no architect or date. The earlier home was the Adliya villa.
funding_verdict: Al Riwaq Art Space: no funder named; the site lists earned income lines (education, space rental, shop, cafe)

name: RAK Art Foundation
overview: Non-profit art foundation in Riffa, in the centre of Bahrain, housed in the converted family home where its founder grew up (foundation website, Identity).

Its founder, Shaikh Rashid bin Khalifa Al Khalifa, born in Riffa in 1952, is an artist, collector and patron who founded the Bahrain Arts Society in 1983 (foundation website) and a member of the royal family and cousin of the ruler (Identity, The Art Newspaper, 2018).

He held the government posts of undersecretary for tourism and culture and for immigration, passports and nationality (The Art Newspaper, 2018). In November 2021 a royal decree named him chairman of the new National Council for Arts, a body attached to the Cabinet (Daily Tribune, 16 November 2021).
funding_verdict: RAK Art Foundation: founder-funded non-profit: the collection and home of a member of Bahrain's royal family, with a US Embassy grant for one residency

press_items.title: Anna Somers Cocks, "Why being a royal artist in the Gulf is a mixed blessing" (2018)

name: Bangladesh National Museum
overview: Bangladesh's national museum on 8.63 acres at Shahbag, Dhaka; officially Bangladesh Jatiya Jadughar.
It began as the Dacca Museum, formally opened on 7 August 1913 by Lord Carmichael, governor of the Bengal presidency (Banglapedia).
A Board of Trustees was formed for the Dhaka Museum in 1970 and a National Museum Commission in 1974.
funding_verdict: Bangladesh National Museum: mainly public: the Government of Bangladesh through the Ministry of Cultural Affairs

name: Fresh Milk Art Platform
overview: Artist-led platform for Caribbean visual artists, with its studio and the Colleen Lewis Reading Room on Walkers Dairy, a working dairy farm in St. George, Barbados (Fresh Milk).

Established in 2011 as a social practice experiment, partly in response to the attrition of BFA students at Barbados Community College, the island's only BFA programme (Fresh Milk). Business Barbados names Annalee Davis as founding director. It began operations in July 2011 and was incorporated as a not-for-profit company on 6 July 2012 (Fresh Milk 2024 financial statements).
Unverified: Wikipedia states that Davis's studio is on a working dairy farm that operated historically as a 17th-century sugarcane plantation. The sentence is unsourced there.
funding_verdict: Fresh Milk Art Platform: grant-funded: Mellon Foundation general operating support, with smaller restricted grants

name: KX Space / Kryly Khalopa Theatre (Prastora KX, closed 2021)
overview: Independent theatre and cultural space in Brest, Belarus. KX Space (Prastora KX) opened in November 2014 as a theatre, gallery and venue for cultural events (the theatre's website, BGmedia).

Founded in 2001 as an activist theatre combining art with critical views on social and political issues in Belarus. Called the Free Theatre (Svobodny teatr) from 2001 to 2011, then Kryly Khalopa (the theatre's website, BGmedia).
Led by director Oksana (Aksana) Gaiko, who calls it the first Free Theatre in Belarus (BGmedia, 8 June 2022).
funding_verdict: KX Space / Kryly Khalopa Theatre: self-funded: workshops, theatre schools and space rentals, according to its director
wider_context: In late January 2021 the financial investigation department came to the space, and Gaiko was taken to the department for questioning after the inspection; a few days later emergency services inspected the premises, and the space suspended all its projects (BGmedia).

On 18 June 2021 the Moscow district administration of Brest liquidated the socio-cultural institution "Theatre Kryly Khalopa" at the Brest prosecutor's request, citing activity that did not match its charter (BGmedia).

A Prosecutor General's Office statement on Telegram, relayed by BGmedia, said the theatre organised exhibitions and art presentations "aimed at forming among citizens an approving attitude to unlawful acts" and engaged in entrepreneurial activity in violation of its statute (translation).

These state bodies acted against the theatre's institution, while its director described the funding as the theatre's own workshops, theatre schools and space rentals (The Theatre Times, 4 November 2019).

name: Art-Siadziba
overview: Independent cultural platform and non-governmental organisation in Minsk that, through concerts, lectures and entertainment events, brought young people across the country to Belarusian language and culture (Radio Svaboda, Kalektar).

Founded on 24 December 2011 (Radio Svaboda); Radio Svaboda names Pavel Belavus as a founder and its first director, and Kalektar lists Belavus as founder with Zmitser Afanasenka and Franak Viachorka as co-founders.
The English Wikipedia entry translates the name as "Art Headquarters"; RFE/RL renders it as "Art Homestead".
funding_verdict: Art-Siadziba: independent non-profit in rented premises; the culture ministry declined to work with it
wider_context: In July 2012, when the space closed for the first time, the city culture department said it does not handle decisions of this kind (Nasha Niva).

Unverified: after the third loss of premises in December 2012, Belavus said the landlord had been summoned to the Minsk city executive committee and strongly advised to cancel the lease, and that the order came from its ideology department; Nasha Niva reports this as his account.

Radio Svaboda reports that Art-Siadziba was put on a list of organisations to be liquidated in late July 2021, after Alexander Lukashenko had announced a purge of non-governmental organisations on 22 July 2021.
By the end of 2021 the authorities had liquidated at least 275 NGOs; by the end of April 2024 at least 1,622 non-commercial organisations had been liquidated, according to Lawtrend (Radio Svaboda).

Amnesty International (Aisha Jung, 22 February 2021): "The authorities are methodically destroying Belarus's spirited cultural life and its most creative members." The statement is about the country's cultural scene as a whole.

Belavus was detained on 15 November 2021 (Nasha Niva), and on 11 May 2023 Judge Zhanna Brysina of the Minsk City Court sentenced him to 13 years for treason, leading an extremist group and other charges; the extremist charge concerned his leadership of the Belarusian Culture Council (RFE/RL).
He was released on 16 September 2026 in a group of political prisoners freed after a US delegation came to Minsk (Nasha Niva).
The liquidation and the founder's prosecution came from the Belarusian state, which did not fund the space.

name: Groeningemuseum
overview: Municipal art museum at Dijver 12 in the centre of Bruges, showing six centuries of Belgian visual art.
One of the 13 city museums and monuments run as Musea Brugge, which the Flemish government recognises as a cultural heritage institution.
Built on the site of the medieval Eekhout Abbey (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Groeningemuseum: public: the City of Bruges, with Flemish government money for the new museum site

name: Argos
overview: Centre for audiovisual arts at Werfstraat 13 (rue du Chantier), 1000 Brussels, in the historic Les Quais district (argos, "Our history" and "visit us").

Founded in Brussels in 1989 to promote the emerging Belgian audiovisual arts scene, first with screenings in cultural centres around Belgium and early distribution of videos to festivals, art institutions and television abroad (argos, "Our history"). The Belgian company register lists the non-profit association (vzw) behind it under the name ARGOS, with a start date of 18 July 1985 (Crossroads Bank for Enterprises).

Since 1999 it has occupied a former storage facility, after several moves around the city, converted in stages into two exhibition spaces, a projection room, a media library, a climate-controlled archive, studios, offices, a café and a bookshop (argos, "Our history").
funding_verdict: Argos: mainly public: the Flemish Community and the Flemish Community Commission

name: Fondation CAB
overview: Non-profit space for minimal and conceptual art at Rue Borrens 32-34, 1050 Ixelles, Brussels, near the Étangs d'Ixelles (Brussels Museums; the foundation's website).
Founded in 2012 by the collector and property developer Hubert Bonnet. He found the 800 m2 former coal warehouse and is involved in its programming (Wikipedia on Bonnet).

Building: a 1930s Art Deco warehouse built for the coal mining industry, restored by the architect Olivier Dwek into an 800 m2 open, modular exhibition space, with a studio for artists in residence (the foundation's website).
funding_verdict: Fondation CAB (Brussels): private: founder Hubert Bonnet's property and finance wealth, with paying members and corporate partners

name: iMAL
overview: Art centre and laboratory for digital cultures and technology at 30 Quai des Charbonnages, Molenbeek, Brussels (iMAL).

Yves Bernard began the project at the end of 1998, named it iMAL (interactive Media Art Lab) in 1999 and launched its first project, CONTinENT, within the European Capitals of Culture programme Brussels 2000 and Helsinki 2000. The non-profit was legally created in May 2000 and he ran it until mid-2021 (iMAL).
Lucía García is the current director (iMAL).
funding_verdict: iMAL: mainly public: Belgian French- and Flemish-community bodies and the EU, with two private partners

name: Z33
overview: House for contemporary art, design and architecture at Bonnefantenstraat 1, Hasselt (Z33).

Evolved out of its predecessor PCBK in 2002. It became an independent non-profit organisation on 1 January 2018, taking over former provincial tasks and the work of four smaller organisations (Wikipedia).
Wikipedia says Z33 was housed in the former beguinage in Hasselt. It moved to Bonnefantenstraat 1 in January 2020 (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Z33: public: the Flemish Community under the Arts decree since 2006 and the Province of Limburg (Wikipedia), with the Nationale Loterij among its partners

name: Image Factory Art Foundation (Imagination Factory)
overview: Art foundation and gallery at 91 North Front Street, Belize City, hosting exhibitions by local, regional and international artists, workshops, classes and residencies (Wikipedia, article on Yasser Musa).

Founded in 1995 by Yasser Musa, a Belizean visual artist, teacher, poet and publisher (Wikipedia; Breaking Belize News, Aaron Humes, "25 years of the Image Factory", 5 June 2020). The 501 Academy page says it started in 1995 and is now called the Imagination Factory, a name used in 2025 for its 30th anniversary.
Musa is the son of former Belizean prime minister Said Musa (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Image Factory Art Foundation: founder-led: free space from a former prime minister

name: Fondation Zinsou
overview: Contemporary art foundation in Benin with two sites: the Ouidah Museum in the Villa Ajavon, behind the Basilica of Ouidah, and the Cotonou LAB, an exhibition space (the foundation's website).

Founded by Marie-Cécile Zinsou, who conceived it in 2003 after noticing that Benin had no structure for contemporary artists. A free exhibition space opened in Ouidah's Villa Avajon in 2005 (Carenews, 11 March 2015). The foundation marks its 20th anniversary in 2025 (the foundation's website).

By 2015 the Ouidah space had hosted 24 exhibitions, and travelling shows had gone to Belgium, the United States and the Paris metro (a 2011 photo project), the foundation had six libraries in working-class neighbourhoods and partnered with 364 schools. The libraries had more than 115,000 readers in 2014 (Carenews, 2015).
funding_verdict: Fondation Zinsou: private patronage: the Zinsou family and a circle of patrons
wider_context: In August 2019 a Benin court gave Lionel Zinsou a suspended six-month jail term and a five-year ban from standing for election, for using false documents and breaking spending limits in his 2016 presidential campaign. Vincent Foly, editor-in-chief of La Nouvelle Tribune, said President Patrice Talon takes seemingly minor decisions that target opponents (Al Jazeera, AFP, 2 August 2019). The article does not mention the foundation.

Lionel Zinsou's relation to the foundation: the foundation's patrons page lists "Lionel et Marie-Christine Zinsou" in its Circle of Major Patrons, and Wikipedia names Lionel Zinsou as Marie-Cécile Zinsou's father. The ruling concerned his campaign, not the foundation.

press_items.title: "[D'AILLEURS] Une fondation culturelle active depuis dix ans au Bénin" (11 March 2015, updated 17 March 2015)

name: Museu de Arte Brasileira da FAAP
overview: Museum of Brazilian art on the São Paulo campus of the Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado (FAAP), at Rua Alagoas 903, Higienópolis (MAB website).

The will of Armando Alvares Penteado provided for a museum. FAAP was established in 1947 and the museum opened to the public on 10 August 1961 with the exhibition "Barroco no Brasil", about 300 pieces. Its first directors were Lucia Comenale and Roberto Pinto de Souza (MAB website). Portuguese Wikipedia dates the opening to 1960 and names his widow as Annie Alwis.
FAAP is a private higher-education institution with campuses in São Paulo, Ribeirão Preto and São José dos Campos (Portuguese Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Museu de Arte Brasileira da FAAP: private: kept by the FAAP foundation

name: FESPACO
overview: Panafrican Film and Television Festival of Ouagadougou, held every second year in Ouagadougou. The 29th edition ran from 22 February to 1 March 2025 and the 30th is scheduled for 20 to 27 March 2027 (FESPACO).
Founded in 1969 and renamed FESPACO in 1972, when a government decree recognised it as an institution. Its top prize, the Étalon de Yennenga, dates from 1972 (Wikipedia).
A new headquarters, begun in 1994, was inaugurated in 2005. Opening night takes place at the Stade du 4-Août (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: FESPACO: mainly public: the Burkina Faso state, with the European Union, the state lottery LONAB and a telecom sponsor
wider_context: AFP, in Le360 on 22 February 2025 ("Burkina Faso: début du Fespaco, grand festival de cinéma africain, malgré le contexte sécuritaire"), writes that since the 2022 coup the junta led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré has silenced critics through arrests, kidnappings and forced conscription.

The Burkina Faso state pays about 70 to 80 percent of FESPACO's executed 2025 budget (Africultures), and Traoré attended the opening and closing ceremonies (Contemporary And). The AFP passage concerns the junta's treatment of critics in general.
